# Query-directed exact suffix repair on the MBTA development projection

Keep the previous Boston network, OD/time batch, cancellations, five repetitions and random method ordering. Give all indexed methods cached base route vectors and a trip-to-query inverted index. The indexed connection-scan comparator builds those routes from exact destination profiles and reruns the original station-based connection scan for affected queries only. The lazy method stores the set of trip IDs along each base optimal suffix as a bit vector. During a deletion, surviving suffixes can reuse their base labels. Compute damaged suffix labels recursively on demand from affected query starts. Memoize by query batch and reconstruct complete journeys. Prune any successor whose original earliest arrival cannot improve the best surviving alternative found so far. Include the identical lazy method without this bound and all five earlier methods. Original event topology and vector-of-rides output apply to every solver. Time copying returned journeys, batch dispatch, solve, and logical cache reset, plus setup amortized over 48 updates. Five randomized repetitions per scenario, one core. Compare per-scenario median p95 and geometric-mean latency before and after amortization. A development pass requires 10% lower latency on all four summaries versus every alternative and exact optimal witnesses. Check against the original independent Dijkstra verifier. A failed development margin leaves the external period unopened. This is an exploratory follow-up on the previously examined MBTA sample.
